In this essay, I will compare and contrast the views of two prominent members of analytic philosophy - Ludwig Wittgenstein and Alfred J. Ayer.
Ludwig Wittgenstein was an early 20th century Austrian-British philosopher, one of the founders of the logical positivists.
Ayer was a British philosopher in the first half of the 20th century who was influential as a member of the Vienna Circle.

Both were associated with the tradition that later became known as logical positivism (also known as empiricist) and also with a group of philosophers that referred themselves as "the Wittgensteinians" but not with the school of thought called "Wittgensteinian".
This essay will be focusing on their contributions to the analytical school.
Both philosophers worked on the foundations of knowledge.
Ayer's book "Language, Truth and Logic" has been considered the first work in logical positivism.

He argued that it was impossible to talk about the metaphysical, because it was impossible to give any sense to such statements, since such statements could not be tested, and therefore were not true or false.
Therefore his point of view can be considered that of a "logical empiricist", which is sometimes confused as "Wittgensteinian".
However, Wittgenstein's approach to philosophy was different.
Unlike Ayer, he thought that philosophy did not need to be based on science.

His aim in writing Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus was not to write a theory, but to write the theory down, and to explain what was wrong with the way of thinking in which there existed other theories.
